svg.text: Tuned configs. Broker on CPUs 0-3, load generator (zzq_brokerbench, raw sockets) on CPUs 4-5. 1 s warmup (rumqttd 5 s, while its message log grows), then 5 s.
Throughput is delivered messages. QoS 1/2 publishers keep 100 in flight; QoS 0 has no flow control, so it can trail QoS 1 at large sizes.
Fan-in: most rivals drop what the subscriber's queue cannot hold, and at QoS 0 EMQX closes the subscriber (mailbox overflow).
VerneMQ acks QoS 1/2 publishes far faster than it delivers them: delivery nearly stops until the publishers do.
zzq on 2 IO lanes: the single pair and the round trip cross lanes. rumqttd speaks MQTT 3.1.1, the rest 5.0. Round trips at QoS 0 and 1 only.
Intel Core i7-8700B @ 3.20 GHz (KVM), performance governor, turbo off
16 pairs: 16 publishers → 16 subscribers, a topic each
round trip, 1 message in flight: p99, whiskers p50 to p99.9
